activities.description: Narrator introduces the Molecule Editor window.
Narrator starts building a molecule by adding Carbon atoms.
Narrator adds Nitrogen and changes its charge to create NH3+.
Narrator changes a single bond to a double bond.
Narrator minimizes the molecule structure for optimization.

characterInteraction.description: The narrator interacts with the software displaying molecule creation and manipulation.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene serves as an introduction to the software, setting up for further exploration of its features.

narrativeProgression.description: Demonstration of atom addition and bond manipulation.

props.name: Molecule Editor Window with a methane molecule displayed.
Atom Manipulation tools including element buttons (C, N) and charge manipulation (+).

scenes.title: Introducing the Molecule Calculator

videoEditingDetails.description: Simple screen recording of the Molecule Editor window.

activities.description: Narrator initiates a calculation on the molecule.
Narrator explores three calculation options: Heat of Formation, Molecular Orbital, and Vibrational Frequency.
Narrator calculates and displays the Heat of Formation.
Narrator calculates and displays Molecular Orbitals.
Narrator calculates and displays Vibrational Frequencies.
Narrator visualizes the lowest vibrational frequency and adds vectors to the molecule display.
Narrator turns off atom display for a simplified view.

characterInteraction.description: The narrator interacts with the calculation options, providing explanations.

trimmingSuggestions.description: The molecule building process could be shortened to focus on the key steps (adding carbon and nitrogen, changing charge).
The vibrational frequencies demonstration could be shortened by showcasing only one frequency and its visualization.
The detailed demonstration of all measurements (distances, angles, dihedral angles) could be condensed by showing one example of each type.
